message:
Prepare the update. Reply with {"messages": [...], "revised_schedule": [...], "volunteer_tasks": [...]} as in the ripple-contracts skill. Do NOT create files: Ripple builds the .ics and .csv itself.
- One message per affected group (effect "inform", "resize" or the disruption origin); "group" = the group id. Say only what changed for that group. status "draft".
- "to": the address of a single person (see the attached people.csv), otherwise a short description like "40 workshop participants".
- The group grp_attendees grew. Do NOT message its existing members. Write one welcome message to the newcomers (group "grp_newcomers") and one to each supplier whose quantity changes.
- "revised_schedule": every schedule item or commitment whose time or place changes: {"id": node id, "start": "HH:MM", "end": "HH:MM", "place": "..."}. Empty list if nothing moves.

messages.body: Hello, following 30 late registrations, the attendee count has grown from 200 to 230. Please update the catering delivery for 12:00 at Salon Jouffroy (Paris Salles) to 230 meals. The dietary split for the additional 30 is not yet confirmed; we will send that separately. Please confirm the revised quantity and any price change.

The contract's unit price and total aren't in my inputs beyond what's listed, so I won't invent a new total; I'll only state the quantity change.
- Do not message existing `grp_attendees` members.
- Schedule/place times do not change: no item's time or place moves, so `revised_schedule` is empty.
- Volunteer tasks: nothing in the inputs requires a new task, so I'll return an empty list rather than invent one.
- Newcomers are "Attendees" joining, so the welcome message is addressed to a description, since no address is given for them.
